series: The TUZ Podcast (The Timeline Unification Zone)

sections.text: stands on a parapet, sketchbook in one hand, field glasses in the other.
(quiet, to himself) The horizon always lies… just beyond the next ridge.A glowing blue-white rift suddenly tears open behind him — the Timeline Unification Zone calling.

stands center stage like a cosmic talk-show host.UNCLE BILLY BOBBY Howdy, friends and fellow timeline travelers! Welcome back to The Horizon Line… and right here in the Timeline Unification Zone — the TUZ!  Today we're pulling in a very special guest. A French soldier. An artist. A man who looked at two empires colliding and said, "I'll stand with the ones fighting for their way of life."  Ladies and gentlemen… Captain Jules Brunet — the real-life French samurai who became the Obi-Wan Kenobi of the Boshin War.A swirling portal opens. JULES
(slight French accent, serene) Uncle Billy Bobby. It is… an honor to stand where all horizons meet.
(bowing slightly, respectful but firm) Emperor. You sent the mission that brought me to Japan. I merely… chose not to abandon it when the orders changed.

(chuckling, gesturing to seats that materialize) All right, gentlemen, let's sit down before the timelines start arguing. Jules — you were supposed to train the Shogun's army and go home. Instead you stayed, fought at Toba-Fushimi, helped found the Republic of Ezo, and became second-in-command at Hakodate. Why?
(leaning forward, intrigued) You defied your emperor. I defied kings. There is a price.

(calm Obi-Wan energy) There is always a price, Emperor. But some prices buy time for others to find a better path. The Meiji Restoration modernized Japan… yet the spirit I fought beside still lives in their culture. I did not lose. I simply… passed the torch across the horizon.
nods and flips pages — vivid sketches of Japanese soldiers, battles, daily life.BRUNET Art is the only weapon that survives every timeline. While cannons rust, drawings speak.

(to Napoleon, with quiet intensity — pure Obi-Wan) You conquered continents with cannon and genius. I tried to preserve a dying code with the same tools. In the end, both of us discovered the same truth:  No empire lasts forever. But the men who choose honor over orders… they become legends that cross every horizon.
(smiling, rare genuine respect) Well said, Captain. Perhaps next time we unify timelines, you advise me.
(small smile) I already did, Emperor. You just didn't listen.
laughs warmly.UNCLE BILLY BOBBY And that, folks, is why we come to the TUZ. To let history talk to itself — and maybe teach us something before we make the same mistakes again.
(rising, sketchbook closed like a lightsaber returning to its belt) The horizon is never the end, Uncle Billy. Only the place where one story meets the next.
(watching him go) Interesting man. I may have to recruit him in another timeline.
(to camera) That's it for this episode of The Horizon Line. Next time in the TUZ… who knows who'll walk through that door?  Until then — keep your eyes on the horizon.
